issues.legal_issue: A claimant who is a co-sharer may claim pre-emption under the residual co-sharer category even if the claimant is also a relative formerly listed in an invalidated kinship-based priority category.
material_facts: The property was jointly held, and a vendor sold a share without all co-sharers joining in the sale.
The claimant was a co-sharer and the vendors’ father’s brother’s son.
The courts below rejected the claim by applying an earlier decision that excluded co-sharers covered by the former kinship-based categories.
The earlier kinship-based categories had been struck down as unconstitutional, while the right of pre-emption based on co-sharership had been upheld.
issues.conclusion: The residual co-sharer category includes a claimant who is a co-sharer even if that claimant is also a relative formerly covered by one of the invalidated kinship-based categories; the contrary interpretation in Jagdish was overruled.
issues.legal_principle: Section 15(1)(b), fourthly, of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, 1913, is a residual category intended to include all co-sharers. In Atam Prakash v. State of Haryana, the Court invalidated the kinship-based priorities in Section 15 while upholding pre-emption based on co-sharership as constitutionally valid under Articles 14 and 15, consistently with the property-right analysis in Article 19(1)(f). The word “other” does not exclude a co-sharer merely because that person also falls within a former kinship category; after those categories were invalidated, “other” is redundant. Jagdish v. Nathi Mal Kejriwal was overruled on this point. Ram Sarup v. Munshi and Bhau Ram v. B. Baijnath Singh were also referred to in support of the validity of co-sharer pre-emption.

predicates.preemption_suit_over_partial_joint_share: A claimant brought a pre-emption suit concerning a share in jointly held property that was sold without all co-sharers joining in the sale.
predicates.claimant_is_a_coshare: The person seeking pre-emption held the property as a co-sharer.
predicates.kinship_based_priorities_have_been_inval: A court had invalidated priority categories that granted pre-emption based on family relationship.
predicates.a_coshare_may_claim_preemption: A claimant who is a co-sharer may claim pre-emption notwithstanding that the claimant also belongs to a formerly specified family category.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption suit concerns a partial sale of jointly held property, the claimant is a co-sharer, and kinship-based priorities have been invalidated, the co-sharer may claim pre-emption.
